sentences.text:
No.8232 Of 2017) vs In Re: Jogaswar Naskar on 6 November,
2024

06.11.2024
 Sl. No.86
 akd
 [Allowed]
 C. R. M. (Db) 3267 of 2024

In Re: An application for bail under Section 483 of the B  Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 filed on 13.09.2024 in connection   Joynagar Police Station Case No.1634 of 2017 dated 29.11.
Sections 498A/302/201/120B of the Indian Penal Code. (G.R  No.8232 of 2017)
 And  In Re: Jogaswar Naskar  ...
 Mr. Ramashis Mukherjee  ... ... for the pet  Mr. Soumik Ganguly  Mr. Dattatreya Dutta  ... ... for the Sta  1.
Heard the learned Advocates appearing for both the parties.
2. We have considered the materials on record.
Petitioner is in custody for over seven years.

As per report submitted before this court in Re: The Court in its own motion, In Re: UTP Dipak Joshi,
lodged in Dum Dum Central Corretional Home1, it appears petitioner is suffering from serious illness.
Purely on medical ground, we are inclined to enlarge the petitioner on bail.

3. Therefore, the accused/petitioner, namely Jogaswar Naskar, be released on bail upon furnishing a bond of Rs.10,000/- (Rupees Ten thousand only), with two sureties of like amount each, one of whom must be local, to the satisfaction of the learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate,
Baruipur, South 24-Parganas subject to condition that the said petitioner shall appear before the trial court on every date of hearing until further orders and shall not intimidate witnesses or tamper with evidence in any manner whatsoever.

4. In the event he fails to appear before the trial court without justifiable cause, the trial court shall be at liberty to cancel his bail automatically without reference to this court.
5. The application for bail, thus, stands allowed.
